demand.missing_reason: No reproducible U.S. sales, panel, conversion, or approved demand-proxy series; marketplace presence and mentions do not establish demand.

competition_gap.missing_reason: Marketplace result pages mix raw and ready-to-eat products, duplicates, and sponsored cards; no approved deduplicated brand-share or concentration transform exists.

margin.missing_reason: Sensitivity scenarios are not quotes; landed cost lacks a supplier quote, freight quote, product-specific tariff ruling, customs overhead, fulfillment contract, and measured breakage.

search_velocity.missing_reason: No reproducible U.S. time series with provider version, date window, and request identity was captured.

social_velocity.missing_reason: Observed recipes, videos, and anecdotes lack a reproducible U.S. time series and cannot be converted from mention counts into demand.

supplier_depth.missing_reason: Multiple suppliers claim capability, but no independent entity verification, quote, certificate, audit, COA, sample, or on-time performance evidence exists.

shelf_stability.missing_reason: No finished, seasoned product shelf-life study or supplier specification tied to the proposed package was obtained.

shipping.missing_reason: Physical research supports fragility and low density, but commercial package dimensions, zone rates, damage tests, and breakage allowances are absent.

brandability.missing_reason: No approved brandability transform or trademark/domain clearance; all three exploratory names have descriptive, prior-use, terminology, or semantic risks.

repeat_purchase.missing_reason: No cohort, reorder, household panel, or measured consumption-cadence evidence exists.

regulatory_risk.missing_reason: General duties are identifiable, but exact formula, claims, facility status, FSVP importer, HTS classification, tariff stack, and APHIS treatment are unresolved.

economics.basis: Four 1 oz packs sold as one DTC order. Retail anchors are observed; every cost input is a deliberately broad sensitivity assumption, not a quote. Scenarios exclude CAC, storage, returns, spoilage, breakage, discounts, tax, overhead, and chargebacks.

scenarios.name: LOW (downside contribution)
assumption_notes: Retail equals four times the observed Whole Foods one-ounce price.
Costs deliberately stress freight, duty, import overhead, and fulfillment.
No product-specific customs classification or fulfillment quote exists.

scenarios.name: BASE (working hypothesis)
assumption_notes: Revenue is a hypothetical four-pack price within observed premium-snack anchors.
Factory, packaging, freight, duty, import, and fulfillment costs are unquoted assumptions.
DTC payment processing is assumed at 2.9% plus $0.30.

scenarios.name: HIGH (upside contribution)
assumption_notes: Revenue equals four $5.99 packs, near observed premium marketplace offers.
All cost inputs require favorable scale and execution and are unquoted assumptions.
The scenario is an upside boundary, not a forecast.

card.executive_summary: Makhana is a real but early U.S. snack niche with visible Amazon, Walmart, and Whole Foods presence, a credible Bihar sourcing story, and premium per-ounce pricing. The evidence does not yet prove U.S. velocity, repeat purchase, scalable contribution margin, supplier quality, or import readiness. This card therefore authorizes only a tightly bounded learning test—not a launch or inventory buy.
card.market: Direct snapshots show 100 Amazon results for 'makhana' and 30 Walmart results for 'phool makhana,' but both mix raw ingredients, ready-to-eat snacks, duplicates, and marketplace offers. A first-page Amazon ready-to-eat sample had a $4.06/oz median ($2.60-$5.69) and 54-review median (0-141); the nonrandom, brand-concentrated sample is descriptive only. Whole Foods confirms one AshaPops 1 oz listing at $4.94/oz. Category maturity appears niche-established rather than empty or mass-market.
card.demand: Existing brands, retailer listings, recipes, and long-running Indian familiarity show that the product is intelligible and sellable, not that U.S. demand is large. No reproducible U.S. search trend, sales panel, conversion series, or repeat-rate evidence was captured. Large India-oriented video counts and raw social mentions were explicitly excluded as demand proxies.
card.competition: Credible brands include AshaPops, Farmley, eatThis, Rani, Karma, Peppy Pops, Nourish, and FIT FOX. Salted/plain, masala/peri-peri, chili, cheese, turmeric, barbecue, mint, and variety packs recur, usually in lightweight pouches. Whitespace may exist in transparent Bihar provenance, measured breakage/quality, and a disciplined discovery bundle, but low apparent brand concentration could equally reflect low category demand.
card.supply: APEDA describes India and Bihar as highly concentrated production sources and a fragmented, labor-intensive processing chain with quality and packaging inconsistency. Multiple Bihar suppliers advertise roasted/flavored private label, 25-50 kg MOQs, nitrogen flush, and export documentation; these are unverified seller claims. No supplier quote, sample, audit, certification, COA, labor due diligence, or freight lane was obtained.
card.regulatory_friction: Importing a seasoned packaged food entails FDA facility and prior-notice considerations, an identified FSVP importer with a written supplier-verification program, formula-specific labeling, and substantiated claims. Makhana itself is not a U.S. major allergen, but seasoning and shared equipment may introduce one. Exact HTS classification, tariff stack, country-of-origin presentation, APHIS treatment, and responsible importer remain unresolved; this is not legal advice.
card.product: The product is shelf-stable in concept, flavor-extensible, portionable, and compatible with discovery bundles. Roasting data support a low-density, more fragile product, creating cube and breakage risk; no finished-product shipping test or shelf-life study exists. Education burden is meaningful because consumers see makhana, foxnut, water-lily seed, and inaccurate lotus-seed language. Repeat purchase is plausible for a savory snack but unmeasured.
card.brandability: The category offers Bihar origin, laboratory/batch, crunch, and discovery territories, but no name is cleared. 'FoxNut Labs' is memorable but partly descriptive; 'Popped Lotus' is botanically inaccurate and has prior descriptor use; 'Lotus Eaters' has obvious commercial use and adverse semantic baggage. Preserve naming flexibility and do not select a permanent mark.
card.content_potential: Strong claim-light hooks include trying every U.S. foxnut brand, blind flavor tests, popcorn comparisons, measured breakage tests, harvesting/processing explainers, Bihar sourcing, supplier comparisons, and recipe experiments. Nutrition, satiety, blood-sugar, weight-loss, anti-inflammatory, or disease-risk claims require much stronger substantiation and label/regulatory review.
top_unknowns: Does a defined U.S. audience convert and reorder at a sustainable rate rather than merely sample once?
What is the formula- and package-specific landed cost after a written supplier quote, freight, broker, duty, and tariff classification?
Can a supplier pass identity, food-safety, quality, labor, documentation, and consistency due diligence?
What shelf life and parcel breakage rate does the finished seasoned product achieve in the proposed pouch and shipper?
Can a non-misleading name and positioning clear preliminary trademark/domain screening without leaning on unsupported health claims?
top_risks: A small visible category is mistaken for whitespace when it actually signals weak U.S. demand.
Low density, fragility, fulfillment, and acquisition costs erase premium shelf-price margin.
Fragmented supply creates quality, food-safety, documentation, labor, and consistency failures.
Botanically inaccurate terminology and crowded/descriptive naming create education and trademark risk.
Import, labeling, allergen, tariff, or health-claim errors delay or block commercialization.
card.cheapest_next_experiment: With explicit purchase approval, spend no more than $150 on 6-8 existing U.S. ready-to-eat packs across at least four brands. Run a documented blind taste/value test plus a repeatable pouch-and-parcel breakage check; record net weights, broken-piece percentage, flavor preference, willingness-to-pay, and unaided terminology comprehension. Do not contact suppliers or publish claims yet. Advance only if the test yields a specific product hypothesis and justifies written quotes and a compliant landing-page interest test.
